title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles became stranded in San Francisco during heavy Fourth of July traffic near the Golden Gate Bridge, with multiple cars running out of battery power while stuck in congestion. The gridlock combined with road closures created conditions where the vehicles could not proceed to charging stations, leaving at least a dozen requiring towing. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks in the street, though no injuries occurred.

The deployment failure here is one of system design: the vehicles were not equipped or programmed to manage extended periods of immobility in high-congestion scenarios, or to navigate away from predicted traffic hotspots before battery depletion became critical. The system appears to have lacked resilience for foreseeable urban events, such as holiday traffic. Better pre-event route planning that avoided congested areas, battery reserves sufficient for extended gridlock, or communication systems to notify passengers of battery risks before stranding would have mitigated the failure.

It is not established whether the vehicles' decision-making around the fireworks incident was a failure of perception, routing, or safety protocols, or what specific conditions made the vehicles vulnerable to battery drain relative to the traffic volume.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets on Saturday following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations near the Golden Gate Bridge. The cars' batteries drained while stuck in severe traffic caused by heavy congestion, road closures, and a large volume of travelers. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, including Jaguar I-PACE models, that required towing. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks set off in the street, though no injuries were reported. A passenger recounted an incident where a Waymo continued driving while someone lit fireworks nearby.

Waymo's spokesperson acknowledged the traffic disruptions and stated the company's roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles. The company indicated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic events. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the incident with public and private partners to improve the experience for future events. This incident follows a December incident when Waymo vehicles stalled during a citywide power outage affecting over 100,000 customers.
